intro.text: Crosswalk is the world’s largest ethically sourced behavioral intelligence platform, powered by 30 million U.S. consumers who opted in through trusted consumer brand partnerships. This collection model is classified as Zero Party Data because consumers knowingly and explicitly opt in, choose what information they share, and authorize the categories of behavioral data collected. By capturing real digital behavior every day, every URL, every session, every signal, Crosswalk provides a living view of audience discovery, engagement, shopping, streaming, search, and fandom, powering Wall Street, Hollywood, brands, and the next generation of AI.

intro.text: Short Form Conversion is Crosswalk's content-to-content attribution platform. It measures how short-form content (TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, Facebook, X) drives audiences to consume the corresponding long-form title, including theatrical tickets, full episodes, full seasons, full films and official streaming pages. Short Form Conversion identifies panelists who first engage with a short-form post and later visit, watch or purchase the long-form destination, then projects that behavior to the U.S. population using a consistent and validated methodology.

runs.text: Short Form Conversion is Crosswalk's content-to-content attribution platform. It measures how short-form content (TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, Facebook, X) drives audiences to consume the corresponding long-form title, including theatrical tickets, full episodes, full seasons, full films and official streaming pages. Short Form Conversion identifies panelists who first engage with a short-form post and later visit, watch or purchase the long-form destination, then projects that behavior to the U.S. population using a consistent and validated methodology.

paragraphs.text: Short Form Conversion begins with two defined sets of URLs: a Short Form (SF) set and a Long Form (LF) set. The SF set is a curated list of public posts across supported platforms that promote, reference or feature the title. The LF set is a curated list of official destinations for the title, such as: • Streaming title pages • Episode and season pages • Trailer pages on official channels • Ticketing pages (Fandango, AMC, Regal and similar) • Studio and network owned-and-operated pages

paragraphs.text: A panelist is counted as a converter when their first observed title-specific SF interaction with a post in the SF set is followed by an observed LF interaction with a destination in the LF set within a defined Attribution Window. The default Attribution Window is thirty days. Custom windows up to ninety days are supported.

paragraphs.text: Conversion is measured on a per-panelist basis using observed behavior, not modeled inference. • A panelist is credited as a converter only once per title, on the first qualifying LF interaction. • Conversion is attributed to the platform of the panelist's first qualifying SF interaction during the window. • Multiple SF posts within the window do not duplicate the conversion. • LF interactions that occur before any SF interaction are excluded. • LF interactions that occur after the Attribution Window expires are excluded.

paragraphs.text: Short Form Conversion produces several standardized metrics: • Unique Views: The count of distinct panelists who view at least one SF post on a given platform during the date range. Deduplicated across posts within the platform. • Duplicated Views: The total volume of SF post views on a given platform during the date range, including repeat views. • Converted to Title: The count of distinct panelists on a given platform who completed a qualifying LF interaction within the Attribution Window after their SF view. • Conversion Rate: Converted to Title divided by Unique Views, expressed as a percentage. Reported per platform and overall. • Cross-Platform Overlap: The share of converters who engaged with SF content on more than one platform during the window. Metric definitions are applied consistently across projects to ensure comparability.

intro.text: CW IQ Ranker is Crosswalk's daily zeitgeist ranking system. It quantifies the cultural and digital momentum of every entity in the Profile IQ universe (talent, brands, titles, platforms, sports teams and trends) on a 0 to 100 scale, refreshed every twenty-four hours. CW IQ Ranker turns observed panel behavior into a single comparable score so that subjects across categories can be ranked, sorted and tracked side by side. It also produces directional companion indices that explain why a score is moving.

paragraphs.text: CW IQ Ranker scores every entity that has an active Profile IQ profile. The roster is derived directly from the Profile IQ catalog and refreshed automatically when new profiles are published or retired. Entities are organized into master categories including Talent, Brand, Content, Platforms, Sport, Trends and more, with a finer-grained subcategory inherited from the underlying profile (for example, ACTOR, QSR, SERIES: NETFLIX, RETAIL, etc). Each entity carries a brand-terms list that defines the canonical names, aliases and URL patterns used to match clickstream activity back to the subject.

paragraphs.text: Every night, CW IQ Ranker walks the Profile IQ catalog and runs a Layer-1 scoring job against the Crosswalk panel for the prior calendar day. For each (subject, day) pair the system records: • Mentions: total clickstream events matching the subject's brand terms • Unique UIDs: the count of distinct panelists who generated a mention • Panel size: distinct panelists active that day, used as the projection denominator • Companion sub-counts: streaming, most-purchased-brand and viewing-platform hits Days are processed oldest first so that each entity's twenty-eight-day rolling baseline is fully populated before the next day's score is computed.

paragraphs.text: The headline CW IQ Score is a 0 to 100 composite that summarizes a subject's daily presence in the panel. It blends four components:

runs.text: The headline CW IQ Score is a 0 to 100 composite that summarizes a subject's daily presence in the panel. It blends f
our
components:

paragraphs.text: • Volume: today's mention count relative to the subject's twenty-eight-day baseline. • Reach: today's unique UIDs relative to the subject's twenty-eight-day baseline. • Momentum: the slope of mentions and reach over the recent trailing window, capturing acceleration above or below trend. • Recency: weighting that emphasizes the most recent days within the window so that breakouts surface quickly and stale activity decays.

runs.text: • Volume: today's mention count relative to the subject's twenty-eight-day baseline.
• Reach: today's unique UIDs relative to the subject's twenty-eight-day baseline.
• Momentum: the slope of mentions and reach over the recent trailing window, capturing acceleration above or below trend.
• Recency: weighting that emphasizes the most recent days within the window so that breakouts surface quickly and stale activity decays.

paragraphs.text: The composite is computed once per subject per day. Each component is bounded so that no single signal can dominate, and the final score is calibrated so that a reading of 50 represents the subject's own steady-state baseline.

runs.text: The composite is computed once per subject per day. Each component is bounded so that no single signal can dominate, and the final score is calibrated so that a reading of 50 represents the subject's own steady-state baseline.

paragraphs.text: Readings above 50 indicate the subject is over-indexing against its own recent history. Readings below 50 indicate it is under-indexing. Because the baseline is per-subject, the CW IQ Score measures movement relative to the subject itself rather than absolute scale. A small entity having a breakout day can register a higher CW IQ Score than a large entity sitting flat, which is the intended behavior for a zeitgeist ranker.

paragraphs.text: All CW IQ Ranker outputs undergo validation and quality-control review before publication. Validation processes verify that naming-term matching is precise, that classification is stable across the version of the rule set in use, that the twenty-eight-day baseline is complete, that panel-size denominators are reasonable, and that the daily job has produced one row per active subject. Quality-control processes support the interpretation and presentation of results but do not create or alter the underlying behavioral observations. Daily snapshots are immutable once published. If an upstream correction is required, the affected days are recomputed end to end and republished with a new generation timestamp.
